topic: Unlocking Planar Graphs: Euler's Characteristic and Duality
target_audience: University students (Computer Science or Mathematics major)

outline.topic: Unlocking Planar Graphs: Euler's Characteristic and Duality
outline.target_audience: University students (Computer Science or Mathematics major)

sections.title: Prerequisite: Defining the Planar Graph
sections.content: Define a planar graph as a graph that can be drawn in a 2D plane without edges crossing. Introduce the basic components: Vertices (V), Edges (E), and Faces (F), where a face is an enclosed region (including the infinite outer region).
sections.example: Visualizing a house shape: 5 vertices, 6 edges, 2 enclosed faces + 1 outer face = 3 total faces.

sections.title: Euler’s Characteristic Formula (V - E + F = 2)
sections.content: Introduce the fundamental theorem for connected planar graphs. Explain that for any such graph, the number of vertices minus edges plus faces always equals 2. Show a quick animation where moving a vertex preserves this constant.
sections.example: A simple triangle (V=3, E=3, F=2) satisfies 3 - 3 + 2 = 2.

sections.title: The Concept of Graph Duality
sections.content: Define the 'Dual Graph' (G*): Place a node in the center of every face of the original graph. Connect two nodes if their corresponding faces share an edge. Explain the inversion: Vertices of G become faces of G*, and vice versa.
sections.example: Imagine a network of rooms (faces) in a maze; the dual graph represents the 'pathway' nodes connected by doors (shared edges).

sections.title: Properties and Mapping
sections.content: Highlight the inverse relationship: V* = F and F* = V. Explain that duality helps solve complex topological problems by transforming a graph into a structurally simpler or more intuitive dual representation.
sections.example: Map a complex circuit board layout (Graph) to its component interaction map (Dual Graph) to minimize signal interference.

sections.title: Synthesis and Summary
sections.content: Briefly recap how Euler's formula provides the 'balance' of the graph, while duality provides the 'mirror' view. Conclude that these tools are essential for VLSI design, cartography, and network optimization.
sections.example: Summarize with an animation of a cube (planar projection) transforming into its dual (octahedron vertices) to solidify the concept of geometric duality.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite: Defining the Planar Graph
lecture_lines: Vertices, edges, and faces define structure.
Faces include the outer infinite region.
animations: Show a simple planar graph with 4 vertices and 4 edges in #FFFFFF.
Highlight all vertices using a pulsing #FF5733 effect.
Highlight all edges using a pulsing #33FF57 effect.

storyboard.title: Euler’s Characteristic Formula (V - E + F = 2)
lecture_lines: V minus E plus F equals 2.
Moving vertices preserves this constant value.
animations: Display the formula V - E + F = 2 in #FFFFFF.
Highlight the variable V in #FF5733 and label with 'Vertices'.
Highlight the variable E in #33FF57 and label with 'Edges'.
Highlight the variable F in #3357FF and label with 'Faces'.
Emphasize the final result '= 2' with a flashing #FFFFFF effect.

storyboard.title: The Concept of Graph Duality
lecture_lines: Place nodes inside each original face.
animations: Draw a planar graph in #FFFFFF and its dual graph in #FFC300.
Animate lines connecting the dual vertices through the faces of the original graph.
Show the dual transformation with a smooth fade-in for the new edges.

storyboard.title: Properties and Mapping
lecture_lines: Faces become vertices, vertices become faces.
animations: Show the mapping of faces to vertices with color-coded arrows in #FFFFFF.
Highlight one face in #FF5733 and its dual vertex in the same color.
Demonstrate the one-to-one correspondence between dual edges and original edges.

storyboard.title: Synthesis and Summary
animations: Display the Euler formula V - E + F = 2 in #FFFFFF.
Summarize the duality relationship using a central diagram showing the original and dual graphs.
Fade all elements to grey #808080 except the final formula to emphasize the key takeaway.
